description: Figures computed here, never by you, from a table's or dataset's rows. min/max of dates are dates; first/last by row order. Kept as dataset d:<id> (xlsx_read reads it; derive from it again); every value lists its source cells; cells left out are counted by reason. where/join/fill without group_by, measures, bins, pivot: the rows (sort, top apply; a count: measures [{fn: count}]).

bins.description: Group by ranges of a number or date column: [a, b), the last [a, b].

coerce.description: Opt in: read numbers or dates stored as text.

doc.description: Document id; not needed for a dataset (d:).

fill.description: After join: each blank of column takes the same row's value of the fill's from column, e.g. {column: "Limit", from: "Default"}. Sources kept, marked filled.

join.description: First, add another table's columns to each row of the outer from, by key, e.g. {from: "t:Issues", on: ["Ref", "Items"], columns: ["Issue"]}. Every row kept (blank if unmatched); several matches: each added cell a list.

columns.description: This join's table's columns to add. Default: all but its key.

from.description: The table (t:) or dataset (d:) to join.

on.description: Two names: [key column of the outer from (the rows joined to), key column of this join's table]. A list cell (a split column) matches by any of its items.

column.description: None: count or share of rows.

pivot.description: A column whose values become columns.

pivot_values.description: The pivot's columns, in this order, written as filter values ("" for the blank cells); a value without rows still gets its column (count 0, other measures blank). Rows of a value not listed are left out and named in pivot_unlisted.

round.description: Decimals, half away from zero; reported values only.

sort.description: By output column (group_by, a measure's as), not input; first decides first. Blanks last.

split.description: After fill: a row per part of column's text, other cells repeated.

top.description: Keep the first rows after sorting.

where.description: Filters, all met. value as JSON writes it: 12.5, true, dates ISO (2026-01-05), percent as the fraction. gte/lte: numbers, dates, times. contains: text, case ignored; eq/in match exactly; contains_any: any of values.

loose.description: Text ignoring case and all white space.

name: xlsx_derive
